candidates.name: Signed half-rank layer kernel and its limiting sign model (rank-layer limit)
paper_items: I25 complementary images at half rank (transverse.tex:258-291)
candidates.statement: For D=2r large and q->inf, the nonnegative mean-one kernels K_xi(Z)=1{rank Z=r, sign Z=xi}/P(.) on symmetric D x D matrices over F_q satisfy E prod_{(i,j) in B} K_{xi_ij}(X_i - Y_j) -> E_eta prod_j prod_{e={i,k} subset j, both active}(1 + c_0 eta_e xi_ij xi_kj) with eta_e independent uniform signs; i.e. integrating out a face 'center' Y_j turns the three point-face incidences into an exact, non-perturbative product of pair-sign factors whose pair signs are the determinant characters of X_i - X_k.

neighbours.relation: K_xi is a normalized class indicator of this scheme
neighbours.verdict: equivalent AS AN OBJECT (I07 alone is N0/N1); the lemma I08 is not in these sources

final.N: N3 (provisional: tests 1-3 pass for I08, test 4 pending)
final.justification: The N3 attaches to the representation change I08(+I25), not to the kernel object I07, which is N0 transfer (Huo-Wan class indicator in L). Function: a nonnegative pairwise kernel whose common-neighbour integrals reproduce, at full (non-perturbative) strength, a hypergraph-type pair-sign model with independent pair signs; this is what the hypergraph counterexamples have for free and what Lovasz's local theorem shows a graph counterexample must achieve far from the constant kernel. No neighbour found that realizes a signed hypergraph model inside a bipartite homomorphism density. Downgrade risks: (a) a strict judge may score it a 'new bridge' (quadratic-form association schemes -> graph densities) built from N0 parts (scheme class, complementary images, Gauss sums), i.e. N2; (b) once the hypergraph parity target (Conlon-Lee-Sidorenko) and 'use a center' are given, half rank may be quickly found (pivot distance 1). Syntactic tininess of K_xi is irrelevant.

candidates.name: Two-branch activation law (M_kappa vs Gamma_kappa, opposite sign biases, one negative corner) with support forcing

family_D.not_transfer: The kernel object is transfer (N0), and the Lagrangian, Gauss-sum and WL tools are transfer. The candidate is the lemma that couples them into a sign model; no existing theorem is imported as its statement.
family_D.correctness_caveat: Unrefereed refutation of a 1986/1991 conjecture. P-C1.equivalence_criterion: Hit: a nonnegative mean-one kernel family on (point, center) spaces such that, after integrating out a center adjacent to several points, the incidence product equals (in a limit, uniformly, at O(1) strength) a product over point pairs of (1 + c * eta_e * xi xi') with pair signs eta_e that are asymptotically independent across pairs; or any construction realizing an exact signed pair-parity model inside a bipartite density via common neighbours. Expert query (e.g. Conlon, J. Lee, Sidorenko, Fox, Wei, Zhao): was 'realize a hypergraph sign/parity counterexample inside a Levi graph via a center kernel' proposed before? Is any algebraic kernel (quadratic forms, association schemes) known to give exact pair-sign models in common-neighbour integrals? This is the main risk to C1's N3.

Generality: does lem:rank-layer hold for any closed 3-uniform complex with each pair in two faces (with the same D_0)? If yes, the device is reusable for other bipartite H (downstream speedup candidates: other sphere/surface Levi graphs, K_{5,5}\C_10 as Moebius strip has boundary pairs in one face, so it is NOT covered; non-p-forcing for further graphs; common-graph or step-Sidorenko questions).

Why half rank exactly? Test whether other rank layers or other association-scheme classes (Hermitian, alternating forms) give the same center-product identity; a positive answer would make C1 a family (strengthens reuse), a negative one sharpens the eureka content to the half-rank choice.
Witness uniqueness: post-release Codex-assisted repos report a second feasible 13-point template class; check whether it is also a sphere triangulation.

The paper never cites the hypergraph non-Sidorenko literature (Sidorenko 1993 is cited only for positive cases; Conlon-Lee-Sidorenko absent). Was the parity route discovered independently by the model?
